name: Shecaniah
overview: Shecaniah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is primarily identified as the father of Shemaiah, highlighting his role within his family line. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Shecaniah means 'Yahweh has taken up his abode,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's presence. This proper name, found in Nehemiah 3:29, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotations.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shecaniah as the father of Shemaiah, as noted in Nehemiah 3:29. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Shecaniah's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his mention in the context of the rebuilding efforts described in Nehemiah. Being the father of Shemaiah associates him with the community involved in restoring Jerusalem, underscoring the generational involvement in God's work. His presence in the text serves to link family lines participating in the covenant community's restoration.
